$comment: The one source for docs/public/ecosystem/index.html. Hand-authored on purpose: packages/engine/lint-ecosystem.ts checks it against the code (paths, members, edges), so the code is the oracle and this file is the subject. How to update it: README.md in this folder.

statuses.label: Partial
statuses.meaning: Some of it works today; the rest is in review or limited to a development build.

statuses.label: Planned
statuses.meaning: Decided or described in the design record, not built.

roles.label: Theming UI
roles.note: Lane A: a person sets the brand by hand.

roles.label: Agent
roles.note: Lane B: a coding agent drives the same engine.

roles.label: Engine
roles.note: The hub. Everything else reads what it generates.

roles.label: Output
roles.note: Files and Figma artifacts the engine's output becomes.

roles.label: Verification
roles.note: Checks that hold the output to its contracts.

roles.label: Code library
roles.note: The path from tokens to coded components.

modes.viewport: An independent viewport axis: type sets per viewport and a layout mode per breakpoint.

nodes.label: Coding agent
nodes.purpose: Any MCP client, such as Claude Code. It themes brands, builds UI from the tokens, and drives the Figma plugin by command.

nodes.label: Shipped skills
nodes.purpose: Task instructions an agent loads: theme a brand, build UI from the tokens, move a Figma file onto Prism3, and author a component definition.
inputs: The engine's behavior, checked by lint-skills.ts

nodes.label: design.md brief
nodes.purpose: A brand brief in Markdown with YAML front matter. It is a round-trip artifact: the studio exports it, and either lane can read it back in. Two dialects are read: the engine's own and the standard design.md.
inputs: Written by a person or an agent

nodes.label: Theme studio (web)
nodes.purpose: The web dashboard at a public URL. A person sets levers by hand or imports a design.md, sees a live preview with contrast checks per mode, and exports tokens or design.md. The engine runs in the browser; there is no backend.

nodes.label: MCP server
nodes.purpose: The engine over MCP: stdio JSON-RPC, no dependencies. An agent lists levers, validates and themes a brand, themes from a brief, scores UI code, and exports files.
outputs: Tokens, contrast results and the decisions log
Written token, metadata and Figma files

nodes.label: Figma MCP scripts
nodes.purpose: Plain Plugin API scripts for the Figma MCP's use_figma tool. They apply a theme and build components with the plugin closed, and carry the plugin's own executors, so both paths write the same file. Runs only against a designated scratch file.
outputs: Variables, styles and components in the file

nodes.label: Engine CLI
nodes.purpose: Compiles a design.md into tokens from the command line. Exits non-zero on a schema violation, a broken alias or a failed contrast contract. An optional fidelity report compares the brief's values with what the engine generated.

nodes.label: Desktop bridge
nodes.purpose: A local MCP server that relays agent link commands to the open plugin over a localhost WebSocket and streams progress back. Only the development build of the plugin may open that socket; the release build has no network access.

nodes.label: Agent link
nodes.purpose: One versioned command protocol for driving the open plugin. Commands arrive through the file's mailbox or the desktop bridge and run through the same handlers as the panel's buttons. Off by default, never persisted, and nothing in a command is evaluated.
outputs: Result envelopes with a verdict and structured data

nodes.label: Figma plugin
nodes.purpose: Runs the studio's UI inside Figma and writes what the engine plans into the file: variables, styles, components and style guides. It also sets up a page per component, updates built sets in place after a dry run, and prunes what the brand no longer has.
outputs: The brand input, saved in the file

nodes.label: Brand input
nodes.purpose: The small input the engine needs: brand colors, fonts and a set of levers. The lever manifest describes every knob once, and the studio, the plugin and the MCP schema all render from it.
inputs: Levers from the studio or plugin

nodes.label: Prism3 engine
nodes.purpose: Generates the whole token layer from the brand input: color ramps and roles, type, space, radius, shadow, motion and layout. Dependency-free TypeScript with no LLM: the same input always gives the same output.

nodes.label: Component definitions
nodes.purpose: One TypeScript definition per component: anatomy, variants, states, token bindings, accessibility and usage prose. Figma sets, component docs and the planned coded components are projections of these.

nodes.label: Agent metadata
nodes.purpose: A *.ai.json file beside each token tree: what each token means, when to use it and when not to, and which pairs it is measured against. It keeps the token files plain DTCG.
outputs: Metadata an agent reads before writing UI

nodes.label: Component docs
nodes.purpose: One Markdown page per component and one components.ai.json, both generated from the definitions. Maintainer notes stay out of both.

nodes.label: DTCG tokens
nodes.purpose: W3C design tokens. Two forms: one canonical tree, and a consumer set of a base file plus one overlay per mode with no build metadata. Two producers: the engine, and TokenPress reading a Figma file.

nodes.label: Variables and styles
nodes.purpose: Figma variable collections with a mode per appearance and breakpoint, plus text, shadow, gradient and grid styles, all bound to the generated tokens.
inputs: Apply theme, from the plugin or the MCP scripts

nodes.label: Motion in Figma
nodes.purpose: Durations and easing curves reach Figma today as number variables in milliseconds. Native TIMING and EASING variables, with springs, are in review in PR #2635.

nodes.label: Figma components
nodes.purpose: A component set per definition, each on its own page, bound to the variables. Update checks first and writes nothing (a dry run), then applies after you confirm. Prune previews before it deletes. Labels and inverse backdrops are drawn around each set as canvas furniture.
inputs: Component plans, through the plugin or the MCP scripts
outputs: An as-built record for safe updates

nodes.label: Style guides
nodes.purpose: Tables drawn onto the file's token pages for color, dimensions, font variables and text styles. Each specimen is bound to the variable it shows, so it repaints when a value changes. A further phase is specified, not built.
inputs: The plugin's Build style guides page
outputs: Pages a team reviews the brand on

nodes.label: TokenPress
nodes.purpose: A Figma plugin, in this repo and published in the Figma Community, that exports any file's variables and styles to DTCG. It runs the opposite direction from the engine and shares no code with it, so its output is an independent check.
inputs: Variables and styles in a Figma file

nodes.label: Contrast contracts
nodes.purpose: Every text, icon and border role is resolved by contrast against its own surface, in every mode, and checked. A failure stops the run; a role below its floor is warned, never silent.
outputs: Pass or fail per pair, returned to the caller

nodes.label: Code scoring
nodes.purpose: Scores UI code an agent wrote against the brand's tokens: the rate of invented tokens, primitive leaks, and contrast for the pairs it used. The score goes back to the agent.

nodes.label: CI gates
nodes.purpose: Every pull request regenerates every committed artifact and runs the full gate list: drift, contrast, naming, prose, builds and round trips. npm run verify runs the same list locally.
outputs: A pass or a named failure

nodes.label: Token contract
nodes.purpose: Names are versioned; values are not. A committed baseline lists the guaranteed token names. Removing or retyping one is a major contract change, and the baseline refuses to move until the version does.

nodes.label: Style Dictionary build
nodes.purpose: A stock Style Dictionary, with no custom code, builds every brand to CSS, SCSS, JavaScript, iOS and Android in CI. It proves the tokens are consumable. No package is published yet.

nodes.label: CSS variables
nodes.purpose: CSS custom properties. Built and checked in CI; not yet shipped as a package a product can install.

nodes.label: Coded components
nodes.purpose: Web components and React components projected from the same definitions as the Figma sets, vanilla HTML and CSS first. Not built.

nodes.label: Storybook
nodes.purpose: Generated stories for each coded component. Not built.

traces.label: A designer themes a brand in Figma

steps.caption: The designer opens the plugin. It runs the same UI as the web studio.
They set brand colors, fonts and levers. That is the whole input.
The engine generates every token from it, the same way every time.
Each role is checked for contrast in every mode before anything is written.
The engine hands the plugin a write plan.
Apply theme writes the variables, then the styles bound to them.
Style guide pages show the result for review.
The agent loads the prism3-theme skill.
It calls list_levers, then theme_brand, over MCP.
The server validates the brand input against the schema.
The engine generates the token system.
Contrast is checked for every role in every mode.
The results go back into the tool response.
The agent reads the tokens, the metadata and the decisions log.

traces.label: A token on its way to code

steps.caption: A brand input enters the engine.
The engine writes DTCG: a canonical tree and a base plus one overlay per mode.
Every token name is checked against the contract baseline.
A stock Style Dictionary reads the files with no custom code.
It builds CSS variables, checked in CI but not yet published.
Planned: coded components bind to those variables.
Planned: stories are generated for each component.

traces.label: Round trip through Figma and TokenPress

steps.caption: The engine generates the tokens.
The plugin receives the write plan.
Variables and styles land in the Figma file.
TokenPress reads them back out of the file.
Its DTCG export must match the engine's own. CI compares the two.

traces.label: An agent builds components in Figma

steps.caption: With the agent link switched on, the agent sends build-components.
The plugin runs it through the same handler as the panel's Build button.
Each definition becomes a component plan.
The sets are built on their own pages. Later updates check first, then apply after you confirm.
The agent reads the result: a verdict and structured data.
The agent sends the UI code it wrote to score_consumption.
The code is read against the brand's own tokens.
Invented tokens, primitive leaks and contrast failures are counted.
The score goes back to the agent, which fixes what it found.
